key_insight: Quantum recurrent neural networks matched classical recurrent models overall for sleep-disordered breathing detection while using far fewer parameters and few qubits.
engineering_relevance: Compact quantum recurrent models offer a research direction for physiological time-series classification, though practical deployment advantages remain unproven.
method: Use a variational classical–quantum recurrent architecture.
Classify breathing time series as apneic or normal.
Compare against classical recurrent neural networks.
evidence_signal: Across multiple real-world datasets of varying complexity, the quantum model performed best on the smallest dataset but slightly worse in the most complex setting.
watch_item: Current quantum hardware and algorithmic limitations constrain practical use; fewer parameters do not establish a computational speedup.
paper_title: Sleep-Disordered Breathing Detection with Quantum Recurrent Neural Networks
